title: Render a Claude Code-imported home session as a Codex 0.156.0 rollout with a kept, changed and lost account
purpose: The home's first cross-harness translation, one named pair and one session: a home session imported from Claude Code is rendered as a Codex rollout that Codex 0.156.0 resumes, in the shape that version writes for its own threads, with every text part, tool call and tool result carried whole, readable thinking carried as text, the thread announcing in band that it is a translation, and an account beside it naming what was kept, what changed shape and what was lost. Codex's own importer of Claude Code files is the recorded baseline: a compaction, not a copy. This brief improves on it and does not adopt it. Nothing above this translation assumes it until its proof holds.
task: Measure first (R1): record what Codex 0.156.0 writes and what it needs to resume, under scratch Codex homes, and take every shape from that recording, never from a source checkout. Then build the Codex profile in crates/lys-home/src/harness/codex (R2 to R6), the codex-render subcommand (R7), the comparison against the recorded rollout (R8), the account written down in RECORD.md (R9) and the resume proof (R10). In scope: one direction (Claude Code-imported home session to Codex), one version (0.156.0), one session per render. Out of scope: Codex to Claude Code; adopting or calling Codex's importer; Pi or any third harness; launching Codex through the launch template; making the Claude Code render deterministic (its random ids for multi-result tool records are a separate defect carded on its own, and this brief's fixture holds none so the hash it stands on is stable). The render writes the rollout under the target's sessions tree and writes no SQLite file: lys-home writes no other harness's database and takes no C SQLite. If R1 measures that 0.156.0 does not replay a rollout that has no state_5.sqlite and thread_history_1.sqlite rows, the index rows are a step of the proof and not of the crate: R1 records the measured answer and the exact sqlite3 statements, and R10 applies them to the scratch home before the resume. Whether Codex can be made to index a rollout it is handed is a later card's question. R1 has three stopping outcomes, each recorded by name in PROOF-CODEX.md and each returning the card to its lead with no crate file changed: 0.156.0 refusing to run without an auth.json; the recording missing a function_call with its output, a user image, a developer message or a compaction record; and a recorded key that no rule values and that 0.156.0 does not write the same in every payload of its kind, or one content part type carrying more than one content_item_kinds value. The translation marker's developer message carries the kind lys.translation_marker, never a kind Codex uses for its own developer parts, unless R1 measures 0.156.0 refusing to replay it, in which case it carries no content_item_kinds key and PROOF-CODEX.md records why. The rollout names the working directory given by --cwd, or the source session header's when --cwd is omitted and the header holds one, and the translation marker says which. A home compaction is carried as 0.156.0's own compaction record behind the carried-compaction marker. Sidechains are carried as spawned threads when R1 measured the 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape; otherwise each is named lost with that reason and carrying them is its own card.

requirements.title: Record the second party: what Codex 0.156.0 writes and what it needs to resume
requirements.spec: Before any file under crates/lys-home/src changes, the builder measures Codex 0.156.0. Every Codex run in this brief uses the Codex binary that answers `codex-cli 0.156.0` to `--version`, with CODEX_HOME set to an empty scratch directory and its working directory an empty scratch directory, and with the API key supplied as the environment variable 0.156.0 reads for an API key, its value read at launch from the operator's existing key file by path, never printed and never written into any file; no auth.json is copied. IF 0.156.0 refuses to run without an auth.json, THEN the builder records under 'Measured before rendering' in PROOF-CODEX.md the line `run: refused without auth.json`, Codex's exit code and the first line Codex printed, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. Otherwise, in the first scratch home, 0.156.0 writes one thread holding at least two user turns, one of them with one PNG image attached, two assistant replies and one tool call written as a `function_call` with its `function_call_output`, and is asked to spawn one sub-agent thread; in the same scratch home 0.156.0 then writes a second thread of one user turn and one reply, on which Codex's own compact command is run once. The builder copies the first thread's rollout, as Codex wrote it, into the fixture directory as `recorded.jsonl`, a spawned child rollout, when 0.156.0 wrote one, as `recorded-child.jsonl`, and the second thread's rollout as `recorded-compacted.jsonl`. IF `recorded.jsonl` holds no `function_call` with a `function_call_output` of the same call_id, or no user message holding an `input_image` whose `image_url` begins `data:`, or no `message` with role developer, or `recorded-compacted.jsonl` holds no top-level record of type `compacted`, THEN the builder records the line `missing from recording: ` followed by the names of what is missing, with the count of each record type and payload type each file holds, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. For each payload type and role of the compared set, and for the `compacted` payload, the builder lists every key the recording carries (the metadata passthrough's keys included) that R4 gives no value rule for; IF such a key does not hold the same value in every recorded payload of that type and role, THEN the builder records the line `unruled key: <payload type>/<role>/<key>` for each, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. IF, within one payload type and role of the compared set, parts of one content part type carry more than one `content_item_kinds` value, THEN the builder records the line `unruled key: <payload type>/<role>/content_item_kinds` for each such payload type and role, creates no file named by R2 to R9, and the brief stops at R1 with the card returned to its lead. The compared set of a rollout is every response_item whose payload is a `message` with role user or assistant, a `function_call` or a `function_call_output`, in file order, excluding a user message whose first `input_text` begins `<environment_context>`. The builder writes `source.claude-code.jsonl`, a Claude Code 2.1.281 file with one record per item of `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set, in order: a user message as a user record with the same texts and, for each `input_image`, an image block whose media type and base64 data are those of its data URL, in part order, an assistant message as an assistant record with the same texts, a `function_call` as an assistant record holding one tool_use with the same name, the call_id as its id and the parsed arguments as its input, and a `function_call_output` as a user record holding one tool_result with the same output. Every record's `timestamp` is the `timestamp` of the rollout record it transcribes, copied as Codex wrote it. Every record's uuid, and every parentUuid that is not null, is 36 characters with a hyphen at positions 8, 13, 18 and 23 and lowercase hex elsewhere. The builder then records the Claude Code render this brief must leave unchanged, made by the lys-home of the commit the branch is based on, in an empty scratch directory `<scratch>`: `lys-home import --home <scratch>/home --claude-code source.claude-code.jsonl --session fixture`, then `lys-home render --home <scratch>/home --session fixture --uuid 7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44 --cwd /fixture/project --model claude-opus-5-5 --version 2.1.281 --out <scratch>/render/7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44.jsonl`. `claude-code-render.inputs.json` holds those values under the keys `session`, `uuid`, `cwd`, `model`, `version` and `base_commit`; `claude-code-render.sha256` holds the SHA-256 of the rendered JSONL file alone, not of its loss account. Next the builder measures, in a second scratch home holding only `recorded.jsonl` at the path under sessions/ that Codex gave it and no `.sqlite` file, whether `codex resume <thread id>` finds and replays it. IF that resume is refused, THEN the builder reads the rows 0.156.0 wrote for the recorded thread in the first scratch home's state_5.sqlite and thread_history_1.sqlite (and thread_spawn_edges when a child was spawned), writes the matching rows into the second scratch home with the sqlite3 tool, outside lys-home, and measures the resume again. The builder then measures whether 0.156.0 replays a developer message carrying the translation marker's own kind: in the second scratch home, with the rows written there when they were needed, it replaces the rollout by a copy of `recorded.jsonl` into which one developer `message` is inserted immediately after the first turn_context record, carrying the keys and metadata passthrough keys of `recorded.jsonl`'s first developer message, its one `input_text` the translation marker of R2 with source session `fixture`, and its metadata passthrough's `content_item_kinds` equal to [`lys.translation_marker`], every later record's `ordinal` increased by one, and runs `codex resume <thread id>` again. In those statements every value that is transcript text is an expression reading it by path from `recorded.jsonl` with sqlite3's readfile and json_extract, never a literal. PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Measured before rendering' section records each fact on its own line as `key: value`, each sqlite3 statement inside a fenced block, and these facts: the base commit; each record type and payload type of `recorded.jsonl` and of `recorded-compacted.jsonl` with its count; the size of its compared set; `recorded-child.jsonl` as `present` or `absent`; the file-name offset, which is the time in the rollout's file name minus its session_meta payload timestamp truncated to the second, written `+hh:mm` or `-hh:mm`; the index-free resume result as `replayed` or `refused`; and, when refused, the exact statements as text, each table and column they write, and the second result as `replayed` or `refused`; and the marker-kind resume result as `marker kind resume: replayed` or `marker kind resume: refused`, followed, when refused, by the line `marker kind: absent, refused on replay`, Codex's exit code and the first line Codex printed. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write a SQLite file from lys-home, SHALL NOT write, copy or read anything under the operator's live Codex home, SHALL NOT take any shape from any source checkout of Codex, SHALL NOT put a user record holding more than one tool_result into `source.claude-code.jsonl`, and the fixtures and PROOF-CODEX.md SHALL NOT hold a credential or any compared-set text.
acceptance: `recorded.jsonl` exists in the fixture directory, its session_meta payload has cli_version equal to "0.156.0", and it holds at least 1 response_item of payload type `function_call` and 1 of payload type `function_call_output` with the same call_id, at least 1 user message holding an `input_image` whose `image_url` begins `data:`, and at least 1 `message` with role developer.
`recorded-compacted.jsonl` exists in the fixture directory, its session_meta payload has cli_version equal to "0.156.0", and it holds at least 1 top-level record of type `compacted`.
`grep -c 'sk-'` over each file in the fixture directory and over PROOF-CODEX.md prints 0, and the fixture directory holds no file named auth.json.

Every uuid and every non-null parentUuid in `source.claude-code.jsonl` matches `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`, and after `lys-home import` of it no entry id in the session `fixture` matches `-r[0-9]+$`.

Every record of `source.claude-code.jsonl` carries a `timestamp` that parses as RFC 3339 and equals the `timestamp` of the record at the same position in `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set, and after `lys-home import` of it no entry of the session `fixture` has an empty timestamp.
The number of user and assistant records in `source.claude-code.jsonl` equals the compared-set size PROOF-CODEX.md records, and that size is at least 6.

`claude-code-render.sha256` holds one 64-character lowercase hex string; `claude-code-render.inputs.json` holds session `fixture`, uuid `7d3c1a52-9b0e-4f6a-8c21-3e5f0a9b1c44`, cwd `/fixture/project`, model `claude-opus-5-5`, version `2.1.281` and a 40-character base_commit equal to the base commit PROOF-CODEX.md names.

PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Measured before rendering' section holds the index-free resume result as the word `replayed` or the word `refused`, `recorded-child.jsonl` as the word `present` or the word `absent` matching the fixture directory, and a file-name offset matching `^[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$`.
WHEN the index-free resume is recorded as `refused`, the section holds at least one sqlite3 INSERT statement naming the table `threads` and a second resume result.

PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Measured before rendering' section holds exactly one line `marker kind resume: replayed` or `marker kind resume: refused`, and holds the line `marker kind: absent, refused on replay` exactly when that result is `refused`.

No `input_text`, `output_text`, `arguments` or `output` string of `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set occurs whole in PROOF-CODEX.md, and every line of its 'Measured before rendering' section outside a fenced block is a heading, a blank line, or `key: value` whose value is a 40- or 64-character lowercase hex string, a decimal count, a path relative to the repository root, a version, an offset, an exit code, the first line Codex printed on a refusal, a table or column name, a `<payload type>/<role>/<key>` triple, a list of the missing names, `absent, refused on replay`, or one of the words `replayed`, `refused`, `present` and `absent`.

WHEN PROOF-CODEX.md records `run: refused without auth.json`, a `missing from recording:` line or an `unruled key:` line, `git diff` of the base commit against the branch lists no path under crates/lys-home/src.

requirements.title: The Codex 0.156.0 profile: the measured shape, marker texts, derived ids and the rollout's place
requirements.spec: Create the Codex profile module. harness/codex/mod.rs carries module docs naming the Codex version measured (0.156.0), the fixture it was measured from and the rule that a shape is valid for that version only, `pub mod` declarations, and a `#[cfg(test)]` `mod <name>_tests;` declaration for each sibling test file, as harness/claude_code/mod.rs does, and nothing else. shape-0.156.0.json holds the values measured from `recorded.jsonl`, `recorded-child.jsonl` and `recorded-compacted.jsonl` that are not transcript text, not ids and not timestamps: `session_meta`, the recorded session_meta payload without id, session_id, timestamp and context_window.window_id, base_instructions kept as recorded because it is the instruction text Codex wrote for its own thread and not transcript text; `turn_context`, the first recorded turn_context payload without turn_id, root_turn_id and current_date; `task_started`, its model_context_window and collaboration_mode_kind; `items`, for each payload type and role of the compared set, the keys the recorded payload carries and the keys its metadata passthrough carries, the prefix of its `id`, the recorded values of `phase` for an assistant message that ends its turn and for one that does not (null where the recording holds no such message), for each content part type the `content_item_kinds` value the recording gives parts of that type, for each function name the recorded `namespace` (none for a name recorded without one), and for every other key R4 gives no value rule for, its recorded value; `developer`, the keys a recorded developer message carries and its metadata passthrough carries, other than `content_item_kinds`, the prefix of its `id`, and `marker_kind`: the string `lys.translation_marker` when R1 recorded `marker kind resume: replayed` and null when R1 recorded `marker kind resume: refused`; `compacted`, the keys of the recorded `compacted` payload and, for each key other than `message` and `replacement_history`, its rule: `constant` with its recorded value when that value is not transcript text, an id or a token count, `id` when the recorded value is a UUID, and `empty` with its JSON kind when the recorded value holds transcript text or a token count; `file_name_offset`, as R1 recorded it; and `spawned_child`, null when `recorded-child.jsonl` is absent, otherwise an object holding the child's session_meta payload without its ids and timestamps and `parent_link`, the JSON pointers into that payload whose recorded value equals the parent's thread id. In `session_meta`, `turn_context` and `spawned_child`, every string equal to the recorded working directory, or beginning with it followed by `/`, holds `{cwd}` in place of that directory. profile.rs loads the embedded shape into a `Shape` value, which every render function takes as a parameter; holds the one supported version string "0.156.0", the mapping name "codex-0.156.0 render v1" and the four marker texts (translation: `[lys translated context] This thread is a translation, not the original session. Source session: <session id>. Rendered by lys-home <crate version> (<git commit>) with mapping codex-0.156.0 render v1. Working directory from <cwd source>.`, where `<cwd source>` is `the --cwd argument` or `the source session header`; authored: `[lys authored turn] A person wrote this reply; no model produced it.`; inherited: `[lys inherited] Carried from session <from_session>: a predecessor's memory, not this session's own experience.`; carried compaction: `[lys carried compaction] This summary was carried from home session <session id>; it is not a compaction of this thread.`); and defines the derived id: a UUID version 7 whose 48-bit time field is a given RFC 3339 timestamp's Unix milliseconds, whose version and variant bits are set as RFC 9562 names them, and whose other 74 bits are the leading 74 bits of SHA-256 over the given seed strings, each followed by one NUL byte. The thread id is the derived id of the home session header's timestamp over the seeds (session id, id of the last entry on the context path); the context window id is the derived id of the header timestamp over (session id, `context_window`). The rollout path is `<target>/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss-<thread id>.jsonl`, every field taken from the header timestamp shifted by the shape's `file_name_offset`; the account path is the rollout path with `.jsonl` replaced by `.loss.json`. build.rs records the git commit the crate is built from as a compile-time value: WHEN a git repository is present, the commit git names for HEAD; otherwise the value of the LYS_HOME_COMMIT environment variable when it is set and not empty; IF it has neither, THEN the build SHALL fail with a message naming LYS_HOME_COMMIT. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write the commit as unknown or empty, and this brief does not change the crate's publish setting. WHEN a version other than "0.156.0" is asked for, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it by name. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT mint a random id, SHALL NOT read the clock or the process's time zone for any value in the rollout, and SHALL NOT take a shape value from anywhere but the recorded fixtures.
acceptance: For session id `s`, header timestamp `2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` and last context entry id `e9`, the thread id is the same string on two calls, parses as a UUID whose version is 7 and whose variant is RFC 9562's, and its first 12 hex digits with hyphens removed are `00dc6acfac00`, the timestamp's Unix milliseconds as 12 lowercase hex digits.

With target `/t`, header timestamp `2000-01-01T15:30:00.000Z` and file_name_offset `+10:00`, the rollout path is `/t/sessions/2000/01/02/rollout-2000-01-02T01-30-00-<thread id>.jsonl` and the account path is the same path ending `.loss.json` in place of `.jsonl`.
Asking the profile for version `0.155.0` returns an error whose message contains `0.155.0` and `0.156.0`.
Every non-blank, non-comment line of harness/codex/mod.rs is a `pub mod <name>;` line, a `pub use` line, a `#[cfg(test)]` line or a `mod <name>_tests;` line.

For every key of the shape's `session_meta`, replacing `{cwd}` with `recorded.jsonl`'s session_meta cwd gives that key's value in `recorded.jsonl`'s session_meta payload; the same holds for `turn_context` against `recorded.jsonl`'s first turn_context payload.
The shape's `file_name_offset` equals the offset PROOF-CODEX.md records, and its `spawned_child` is null exactly when `recorded-child.jsonl` is absent from the fixture directory.
In the repository, with LYS_HOME_COMMIT unset, the commit the translation marker carries equals the output of `git rev-parse HEAD`.

With GIT_DIR set to a path that does not exist and LYS_HOME_COMMIT set to `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`, `cargo build -p lys-home` exits 0 and the translation marker carries `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`.
With GIT_DIR set to a path that does not exist and LYS_HOME_COMMIT unset, `cargo build -p lys-home` exits non-zero and its output contains `LYS_HOME_COMMIT`.

The shape's `compacted` names every key of `recorded-compacted.jsonl`'s first `compacted` payload, and each key other than `message` and `replacement_history` carries exactly one of the rules `constant`, `id` and `empty`.
The shape's `developer.marker_kind` equals the string `lys.translation_marker` when PROOF-CODEX.md records `marker kind resume: replayed`, and is null when it records `marker kind resume: refused`.

requirements.title: The account: kept, changed and lost, by entry id and block hash
requirements.spec: Define the account written beside a rollout as one JSON object: `source_session` (the home session id), `thread_id`, `mapping` ("codex-0.156.0 render v1"), `rollout` (its path), `child_rollouts` (one object per spawned child rollout, with `thread_id` and `rollout`; empty when there is none), and three arrays of rows. Every row carries `entry_id`, `part` (the part's index in the entry's content, or null for a whole entry), `hash`, `hash_kind` and `blocks`. `kept`: one row per part carried as the Codex item native to its kind with its content unchanged, adding `kind` (the home part kind) and `item` (the Codex item or part kind it became). `changed`: one row per part or entry carried in another kind or with something removed or added, adding `before`, `after` and `how` (a fixed phrase naming the change, never content). `lost`: one row per part or entry not carried, adding `kind` and `reason` (a fixed phrase, never content). Hashes: where the entry names a block hash for the part, `hash` is that block hash and `hash_kind` is `block`, never a second hash of the same bytes; where the part is held inline in the entry with no block named, `hash` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of the part as parsed from the entry and `hash_kind` is `inline`; a whole entry's `hash` is the SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of the entry, `inline`. `blocks` lists, in the order the entry names them, every block hash the entry names for that part or entry (for a lys.call entry its request parts, response parts, raw request and raw response), and is empty otherwise. The account reads what the entry names and does not change how any entry is imported. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write any transcript text, argument, output or thinking into the account, SHALL NOT give a `block` hash that does not resolve in the home's blocks store, SHALL NOT list one part in two arrays, and SHALL NOT omit a part or entry of the context path from all three.
acceptance: An account built for an entry `e1` with parts [text, thinking with signature, redacted thinking] lists part 0 in `kept` with kind `text` and item `output_text`, part 1 in `changed` with before `thinking` and after `output_text`, and part 2 in `lost` with kind `thinking` and reason `redacted thinking: opaque to another provider`; the three rows together number 3.
The `hash` for part 0 equals the SHA-256 of `serde_json::to_vec` of that part as the entry holds it, and its `hash_kind` is `inline` and its `blocks` is empty.

A lys.call entry naming 2 request parts and a raw response, each put in the home's block store, is listed once in `lost` with `blocks` holding those 3 hashes in that order, and `BlockStore::get` returns the stored bytes for each.
The serialised account for a fixture whose texts each contain the string `CANARY-7f3a` contains 0 occurrences of `CANARY-7f3a`.

requirements.title: Home entries into Codex items, carried whole
requirements.spec: Map each context-path entry to Codex 0.156.0 records, each payload carrying exactly the keys the shape records for its payload type and role, valued as follows. `id` is the recorded prefix followed by the derived id of the entry's timestamp over (session id, entry id, part index in decimal). The metadata passthrough carries exactly the keys the shape records for that payload type and role: `turn_id` is the turn R5 places the item in; `create_time` is the entry's timestamp as Unix seconds with its milliseconds as the fraction; `content_item_kinds` holds one value per content part, in part order, each the value the shape records for that part's type. A `function_call`'s `namespace` is the one the shape records for its name, and the key is absent when the shape records none for that name. Every other key the shape records for the payload type and role is written with the value the shape records for it. An assistant message carries the shape's `phase` for a message that ends its turn when it is the last assistant message of its turn and the other recorded `phase` otherwise, and no `phase` key when that value is null. A user message becomes a `message` with role user and one `input_text` per text part, the text byte-identical. An assistant message becomes, in part order: consecutive text and readable-thinking parts gathered into one `message` with role assistant and one `output_text` per part, and each toolCall part a `function_call` with `name` the tool name, `call_id` the tool call id and `arguments` a JSON text whose parsed value equals the toolCall's arguments value; writing the value as text is the only change, as Codex's own function_call carries arguments. A toolResult message becomes a `function_call_output` with `call_id` the tool call id; WHEN the toolResult holds exactly one part and it is text, `output` is that text as a string, byte-identical; otherwise `output` is a list with one `input_text` per text part, byte-identical, and one `input_image` per image part with `image_url` the data URL `data:<media type>;base64,<data>`, in part order. An image part in a user message becomes an `input_image` in the same way. WHEN a thinking part carries readable text, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry that text as an `output_text` and list it as changed (before `thinking`, after `output_text`, how `signature dropped` when it had one and `carried as text` when it had none); IF a thinking part is redacted or its text is empty, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL drop it and list it as lost by hash with reason `redacted thinking: opaque to another provider` or `empty thinking` respectively. WHEN an assistant message's model is `authored`, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it as an assistant message whose first `output_text` is the authored marker and list it as changed with how `authored marker added`; an assistant message whose model is not `authored` carries no authored marker. A lys.authored entry produces no item and is listed as changed with how `carried as the authored marker`. WHEN a user or assistant message's entry id is one of the `from_entries` of a lys.inherited entry on the context path that names a `from_session`, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it in its own role with the inherited marker, naming that `from_session`, as its first text part, and list it as changed with how `inherited marker added`. A lys.inherited entry produces no item and is listed as changed with how `carried as the inherited marker` when it names a `from_session` and `carried as the authored marker` when it does not. WHEN a toolResult has isError true, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry it and list it as changed with how `is_error flag not carried`. A compaction entry becomes one top-level record of type `compacted` whose payload carries exactly the keys the shape's `compacted` records: `message` is the carried-compaction marker with the session id filled in, two newline characters, then the summary byte-identical; `replacement_history`, when recorded, is a list of one user `message` written as this requirement writes one, whose one `input_text` is that same text; every other key is valued by its recorded rule, `constant` its recorded value, `id` the derived id of the compaction entry's timestamp over (session id, compaction entry id, key name), `empty` the empty value of its recorded JSON kind. It is listed as changed with before `compaction`, after `compacted` and how `carried as a Codex compaction record with the carried-compaction marker`. A lys.harness_event, lys.call or any other lys custom entry, a label, and every other entry type are lost with a reason naming the entry type or customType; a part kind with no Codex item is lost with a reason naming the kind. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT drop a lys.authored or lys.inherited entry as lost, SHALL NOT render a compaction entry as a user message, SHALL NOT write a key the shape does not record for that payload type and role, SHALL NOT truncate, clip or summarise any text, argument or output, SHALL NOT change the JSON value of any argument, SHALL NOT write a `reasoning` item, and SHALL NOT write any signature or redacted data into an item.
acceptance: A toolResult whose one text part is 10,000 characters becomes a `function_call_output` whose `output` is a string of 10,000 characters with the same SHA-256 as the source text.
A toolCall with arguments `{"timeout":5,"command":"ls -la"}` becomes a `function_call` whose `arguments`, parsed, equals that JSON value and whose `call_id` equals the toolCall id.

An assistant entry [signed thinking `look first`, text `done`] becomes one assistant `message` with two `output_text` parts, `look first` then `done`, and no item in the output contains the signature string.

A context path of 6 assistant messages with model `authored` followed by 1 assistant message with model `claude-opus-5-5` gives 7 assistant messages: each of the first 6 has first `output_text` equal to `[lys authored turn] A person wrote this reply; no model produced it.`, the 7th holds no `output_text` equal to it, and the account lists the first 6 in `changed` and none of them in `lost`.

A toolResult holding one text part and one image part with media type `image/png` becomes a `function_call_output` whose `output` is a list of an `input_text` then an `input_image` whose `image_url` begins `data:image/png;base64,`.
A user message listed in a lys.inherited entry with from_session `s0` stays role user and its first `input_text` equals the inherited marker with `<from_session>` replaced by `s0`.

A lys.harness_event entry, a label entry and a `document` part each appear once in the account's `lost` with a reason naming `lys.harness_event`, `label` and `document` respectively, and produce no item.

With a Shape recording, for an assistant message, the metadata passthrough keys `turn_id` and `content_item_kinds` and no `create_time`, an assistant message's metadata passthrough has exactly the keys `turn_id` and `content_item_kinds`; with a Shape recording `user.text` for a user `input_text`, a user message of 2 text parts has `content_item_kinds` equal to [`user.text`, `user.text`].

A toolCall named `Bash`, with a Shape recording namespace `ns1` for `exec` and none for `Bash`, becomes a `function_call` with no `namespace` key; a toolCall named `exec` becomes one whose `namespace` is `ns1`.

A compaction entry with summary `SUMMARY-1` becomes one `compacted` record whose payload's keys equal the shape's `compacted` keys and whose `message` equals the carried-compaction marker with the session id filled in, then `\n\n`, then `SUMMARY-1`; no response_item `message` holds `SUMMARY-1`, and the account lists the entry in `changed` with before `compaction` and after `compacted`.

requirements.title: Render the context path to a rollout beside its account
requirements.spec: WHEN codex-render is asked for a session, a target directory and a working directory with its source (the --cwd argument or the source session header, as R7 resolves them), THE SYSTEM SHALL walk the session's context path as the Claude Code render does (Session::context_path) and write the rollout at the R2 path. Turns: a turn opens at each context-path entry that is a user message entry or a compaction entry and at the first rendered entry when that is not one, and closes before the next opening or at the path's end; each turn's id is the derived id of its opening entry's timestamp over (session id, opening entry id). Records, in order: a session_meta record whose payload is the shape's `session_meta` with `{cwd}` replaced by the working directory, and id and session_id the thread id, timestamp the header timestamp, and context_window.window_id the context window id; then for each turn an event_msg `task_started` (turn_id and root_turn_id the turn id, started_at the opening entry's timestamp in Unix seconds, and the shape's `task_started` values), a turn_context record (the shape's `turn_context` with `{cwd}` replaced by the working directory, turn_id and root_turn_id the turn id, and current_date the opening entry's date shifted by the shape's `file_name_offset`), the turn's R4 records in path order, and in the first turn only a developer `message` whose one `input_text` is the translation marker with the source session id, the crate version, the build commit and the working directory's source filled in, carrying the keys the shape's `developer` records valued as R4 values them, with its metadata passthrough's `content_item_kinds` equal to [`lys.translation_marker`] when the shape's `developer.marker_kind` is that string and with no `content_item_kinds` key when it is null, placed immediately after the turn's `compacted` record when the turn opens at a compaction entry and before the turn's first R4 record otherwise; then an event_msg `task_complete` (turn_id; started_at; completed_at the turn's last entry's timestamp in Unix seconds; duration_ms that timestamp minus the opening one in milliseconds; time_to_first_token_ms the first assistant entry's timestamp in the turn minus the opening one in milliseconds, 0 when the turn has none; last_agent_message the last `output_text` of the turn's last assistant message, byte-identical, null when the turn has none). Every record carries exactly the top-level keys `timestamp`, `ordinal` (its 0-based line index), `type` and `payload`; `timestamp` is written `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.mmmZ` in UTC and is the header timestamp for session_meta, the opening entry's for task_started, turn_context and the marker, the turn's last entry's for task_complete, and the source entry's for an R4 record. Then THE SYSTEM SHALL write the R3 account at the R2 account path. IF the working directory is empty, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the render naming `--cwd` and SHALL create no file. IF the rollout path or the account path exists, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return HomeError::Exists naming that path and SHALL create no file and no directory. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write under any directory but the target, SHALL NOT write any SQLite file, SHALL NOT give the developer marker message a `content_item_kinds` value that Codex 0.156.0 records for its own developer parts, SHALL NOT write a token_count, token_usage_record, item_completed, realtime_item or world_state record, and SHALL NOT append to, open for writing or rewrite any file of the home.
acceptance: Rendering the same session twice to one target: the second call returns HomeError::Exists whose path equals the first call's rollout path, and a listing of every file under the target with its size and SHA-256 is identical before and after the second call.
With only the account path pre-created as an empty file, the call returns HomeError::Exists naming the account path and no rollout file exists afterwards.

For a path [user, assistant, user, assistant] the rollout's record types in order are session_meta, event_msg task_started, turn_context, response_item developer message, user message, assistant message, event_msg task_complete, event_msg task_started, turn_context, user message, assistant message, event_msg task_complete, and each record's `ordinal` equals its line index.
The developer message's text contains the source session id and `codex-0.156.0 render v1`, and the session_meta payload's id equals the thread id in the rollout's file name.
Two renders of one session to two empty targets produce rollouts with the same SHA-256.
The home session file, its index and its head file have the same SHA-256 before and after a render, and the home's blocks directory holds the same file count.
No file whose name ends `.sqlite` exists under the target after a render.

For a path [compaction, user, assistant] the first turn's records after its turn_context are, in order, the `compacted` record, the developer marker message, the user message and the assistant message.

Rendered with working directory `/fixture/project` from the --cwd argument, the session_meta payload's and every turn_context payload's `cwd` equal `/fixture/project` and the developer message's text ends `Working directory from the --cwd argument.`; rendered with working directory `/w` from the source session header, it ends `Working directory from the source session header.`

With a Shape whose `developer.marker_kind` is `lys.translation_marker`, the developer marker message's metadata passthrough `content_item_kinds` equals [`lys.translation_marker`]; with a Shape whose `developer.marker_kind` is null, its metadata passthrough has no `content_item_kinds` key.

requirements.title: Sidechains as spawned threads, in the measured shape
requirements.spec: A sidechain is the entry a label entry names by `targetId` when its label begins `agent `, together with every entry descending from it; sidechain.rs finds them by reading the home session file line by line, read-only, and keeps file order. WHILE the shape's `spawned_child` is not null, THE SYSTEM SHALL render each sidechain as its own child rollout under the target: its thread id is the derived id of the sidechain's first entry's timestamp over (session id, first sidechain entry id); its path follows the R2 rule from that timestamp and thread id; its session_meta payload is `spawned_child`'s payload with `{cwd}` replaced, id and session_id the child's thread id, and the parent's thread id written at each of `parent_link`'s pointers; its turns and items follow R5 and R4 over the sidechain's entries, without the translation marker. The account lists each sidechain part as kept, changed or lost as R4 rules, lists the label entry as changed with how `carried as a spawned thread's parent link`, and names each child in `child_rollouts`. IF `spawned_child` is null, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL write no child rollout and list each sidechain entry and its label in `lost` with reason `sidechain: 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape not measured here`. codex/render.rs calls this step after the parent's items, and checks every child rollout path for existence, refusing as R5 does, before it writes any file. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT write a thread_spawn_edges row or any SQLite file, and SHALL NOT place a sidechain's items in the parent rollout.
acceptance: With a Shape whose `spawned_child` is `{"session_meta": {"parent": ""}, "parent_link": ["/parent"]}`, a fixture session with one sidechain of 2 message entries renders to 2 rollout files under the target, the child's session_meta payload at `/parent` equals the parent rollout's thread id, and the account's `child_rollouts` holds 1 object whose `rollout` is the child's path.

With the same fixture and a Shape whose `spawned_child` is null, the render writes 1 rollout file and the account's `lost` holds 3 rows, the 2 sidechain entries and their label, each with reason `sidechain: 0.156.0 spawned-thread shape not measured here`.
In both cases the parent rollout holds 0 items whose `id` is derived from a sidechain entry id.
With the child rollout path pre-created, the render returns HomeError::Exists naming that path and the parent rollout does not exist afterwards.

requirements.title: The codex-render subcommand and its report
requirements.spec: Add the `codex-render` subcommand with `--home`, `--session`, `--target` (the directory the rollout is written under, which the proof uses as the Codex home) and `--codex-version`, all required, and `--cwd`, the working directory the rollout names. WHEN `--cwd` is given, THE SYSTEM SHALL render with it and name its source as the --cwd argument; WHEN `--cwd` is omitted and the home session header's cwd is not empty, THE SYSTEM SHALL render with the header's cwd and name its source as the source session header; IF `--cwd` is omitted and the header's cwd is empty, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL exit with code 2 and a message naming `--cwd`, as clap does for the other missing arguments, and SHALL create no file. Its argument struct and run function live in harness/codex/command.rs; cli.rs gains only the enum variant and one dispatch arm. WHEN it succeeds, THE SYSTEM SHALL print one JSON object: `command` (`codex-render`), `rollout` (path), `account` (path), `entries` (context-path entries walked), `blocks` (parts walked), `kept`, `changed` and `lost` (the account's array lengths), and `child_rollouts` (paths). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT print, log or put in an error any transcript text, argument, output, thinking or marker text, SHALL NOT launch Codex or any other program, SHALL NOT invent a working directory or render with an empty one, and SHALL NOT change the working directory the importer writes into a home session header.
acceptance: `lys-home codex-render --home H --session fixture --target T --codex-version 0.156.0 --cwd /fixture/project` on the R8 fixture home prints one JSON object whose keys are exactly command, rollout, account, entries, blocks, kept, changed, lost and child_rollouts, and whose kept, changed and lost equal the lengths of the account file's `kept`, `changed` and `lost` arrays.
Omitting `--codex-version` exits with code 2 and the message names `--codex-version`.
On the R8 fixture home, whose session header cwd is empty, the same command without `--cwd` exits with code 2, its message names `--cwd`, and T holds no file afterwards.
On a home whose session header cwd is `/w`, the command without `--cwd` succeeds and the rollout's session_meta `cwd` is `/w`; with `--cwd /x` it is `/x`.
The report's JSON for a fixture whose texts contain `CANARY-7f3a` holds 0 occurrences of `CANARY-7f3a`.
cli.rs and command.rs each hold at most 500 lines of code excluding comments, blank lines and tests.

requirements.title: The fixture comparison against the rollout Codex wrote
requirements.spec: An integration test imports `source.claude-code.jsonl` into a temporary home as session `fixture`, renders it with codex-render to a temporary target with `--cwd /fixture/project`, and compares the rendered rollout's compared set, taken after the translation marker, with `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set as R1 defines it. Two payloads are equal when they are equal as JSON after `id` and `call_id` and the metadata passthrough's `turn_id` and `create_time` are removed from both, with `arguments` compared as parsed JSON values. A second test renders a session holding one signed readable thinking block and one redacted thinking block. A third makes the Claude Code render of the fixture with the values in `claude-code-render.inputs.json`, `--out` under a temporary directory, and compares the rendered JSONL file's SHA-256 with `claude-code-render.sha256`. A fourth changes one `output_text` of an in-memory copy of `recorded.jsonl` and runs the comparison of the first test on it. Test names carry no transcript text. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT compare a set without asserting its length, and SHALL NOT build the expected side from lys-home's own output.
acceptance: The comparison test asserts both compared sets have the length PROOF-CODEX.md records for `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set, which is at least 6, and that every pair is equal.

The thinking test asserts the signed block's text appears as an `output_text`, the account's `changed` names it with before `thinking` and after `output_text`, the account's `lost` names the redacted block with hash_kind `inline`, the SHA-256 of its part and reason `redacted thinking: opaque to another provider`, and the rollout contains neither signature string.
The Claude Code render test's SHA-256 equals the value in `claude-code-render.sha256`.
The fourth test asserts the comparison reports exactly 1 unequal pair.

requirements.title: The loss account written down in the record
requirements.spec: Replace the stub under 'The loss account' in docs/design/home/RECORD.md with the account's fields as R3 defines them, the fixed `how` and `reason` phrases R4, R5 and R6 use, what `hash_kind` `block` and `inline` mean and how a reader recomputes each (a `block` hash from the home's blocks store; an `inline` hash from the home file by entry id and part index), and the Codex importer baseline it is measured against (thinking, sidechains and meta records dropped; tool notes clipped at 2,000 and results at 4,000 characters). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT quote any transcript text and SHALL NOT change what the section says of the Claude Code render's own account.
acceptance: RECORD.md's 'The loss account' section names each of source_session, thread_id, mapping, rollout, child_rollouts, kept, changed, lost, hash_kind and blocks, and every `how` and `reason` phrase that appears in harness/codex/items.rs, render.rs and sidechain.rs appears in it verbatim.
The section no longer contains the words `Written with R4`.

requirements.title: The resume proof on Codex 0.156.0 under a scratch home
requirements.spec: The builder renders the fixture session with codex-render into an empty scratch directory, with `--cwd` the scratch working directory Codex then runs in. WHEN R1 recorded the index-free resume as `refused`, the builder writes the index rows for this thread into that directory with the sqlite3 tool, using R1's recorded statements with this thread's id and rollout path, every transcript value read by path from the rendered rollout, and records them as text under 'Resume'. It then runs Codex 0.156.0 as R1 does, with CODEX_HOME set to that directory, resumes the thread by its id, and asks two questions: the source session id the thread names, and one fact that appears only in the fixture conversation. PROOF-CODEX.md records under 'Resume', each fact on its own line as `key: value` as R1 lays them out: the binary's version answer; the command, naming the key's environment variable and never its value; the SHA-256 of the rollout before and after the resume; the SHA-256 of the home session file before and after; record and item counts; whether R1's statements were `applied` or `not needed`; and for each question the SHA-256 of the expected answer, the SHA-256 of the answer given, and `equal` or `not equal`. IF 0.156.0 refuses to resume without an auth.json, THEN the proof records the line `resume: refused without auth.json`, Codex's exit code and the first line Codex printed as the measured limit, in place of the two answers. PROOF-CODEX.md SHALL NOT hold a question, an answer, any transcript text or a credential, and SHALL NOT name a path under the operator's live Codex home.
acceptance: PROOF-CODEX.md's 'Resume' section names version `0.156.0`, holds a rollout SHA-256 before and after, states the home session file's SHA-256 before and after as equal, and holds the word `applied` or the words `not needed`.

The section holds, for each of the two questions, an expected-answer hash, a given-answer hash and the result `equal`; WHEN it instead holds `resume: refused without auth.json`, it holds an exit code on the same or next line and no answer hash.

`grep -c 'sk-'` over PROOF-CODEX.md prints 0, `grep -c '/.codex/'` over it prints 0, no `input_text`, `output_text`, `arguments` or `output` string of `recorded.jsonl`'s compared set or of the rendered rollout occurs whole in it, and every line of its 'Resume' section outside a fenced block is a heading, a blank line, or `key: value` whose value is a 64-character lowercase hex string, a decimal count, a path relative to the scratch directory, a version, an exit code, the command with the key's environment variable named, the first line Codex printed on a refusal, or one of the words `applied`, `not needed`, `equal` and `not equal`.

boundaries: No file under a live Codex home or a live Claude Code home is written, copied, read for writing or rewritten; everything Codex runs with has CODEX_HOME set to a scratch directory, and the Claude Code render of R1 and R8 writes only under a scratch directory through --out.
No credential and no auth.json is copied into the target, a scratch home or any fixture; the API key is supplied at launch as an environment variable and never printed.
No Codex code is adopted, vendored, depended on or called by lys-home, and Codex's importer of Claude Code files is not run; lys-home builds and tests with no Codex installed.
The codex-render subcommand never launches Codex or any other program.
No change to harness/claude_code/render.rs or harness/claude_code/import.rs, and the Claude Code render's output is not changed.
No home session file, index, head or block is written by the Codex render, and Pi's grammar gains no field or entry kind.
No SQLite file is written by lys-home and no dependency that is not pure Rust is added.
No Codex to Claude Code path, no Pi or third harness, no launch-template change.
No transcript text, argument, output, thinking or marker text in the report, an error, a log line, a test name, the account or PROOF-CODEX.md.
No shape is taken from any source checkout of Codex; every shape comes from the files 0.156.0 wrote in R1.
